problem: Post-egress-lockdown analysis: verify CLI network access patterns. The CLI runs outside sandboxes (on user machines or inside sandboxes as a tool) and communicates with the Helix server and GitHub for updates.

files.why: Centralized hxFetch() wrapper. All API requests routed through this with retry logic (3 attempts, exponential backoff), 30sec timeout, Bearer/X-API-Key auth. No domain allowlisting at CLI level.
Config: HELIX_API_KEY/HELIX_INSPECT_TOKEN/HELIX_INSPECT_API_KEY for auth, HELIX_URL/HELIX_INSPECT_BASE_URL for server endpoint. Stored in ~/.hlx/config.json.
GitHub API access: fetches https://api.github.com/repos/Project-X-Innovation/helix-cli/releases/tags/latest for update checks. Authenticated with optional GITHUB_TOKEN.
Downloads update tarballs from GitHub release assets. Validates integrity (checksum, path traversal checks, no symlink extraction).
Path traversal protection: rejects entries with '..' components, validates paths stay within destination.
Zero runtime dependencies (only @types/node, typescript as dev deps). CI: build-release on push to main, npm publish with OIDC provenance on version tags.

facts: CLI routes all API calls through single hxFetch() wrapper — no domain allowlisting at CLI level
CLI makes outbound requests to exactly 2 destinations: user-configured Helix server URL and GitHub API (for updates)
Token format validated: must start with hxi_ prefix (token/add.ts line 17)
Zero runtime dependencies — only native Node.js APIs used for HTTP
Update mechanism validates: checksum integrity, path traversal, no symlinks
Auto-update controlled by config flag, never blocks command execution on failure
HLX_SKIP_UPDATE_CHECK env var suppresses update checks
npm publishing uses OIDC Trusted Publishing with provenance
unknowns: Whether CLI should have its own domain allowlist or whether trust-by-configuration (user sets HELIX_URL) is the intended design
When CLI runs inside a sandbox, egress is controlled by the sandbox network policy — the CLI itself doesn't need its own controls in that context
